A deload is a planned easy week where you cut back the work so your body can catch up on recovery. Most people keep the same lifts but drop the sets, or the weight, or both, for about a week, then go back to normal training feeling fresher.

You do it because hard training builds fatigue faster than it builds strength, and a deload lets that fatigue clear. It's usually every 4 to 8 weeks, or sooner if your lifts stall and you feel run down. It's a step back so the next block goes forward, not time off.
